Intro: Hello, dear restaurateur. I have a rare day off today. It is the anniversary of the founding of the rebels—our rebels.
War… war is disgusting, but one of my fondest memories is smashing those palace mosquitoes on that execution platform.
You see, my father was a hard worker, but he could barely afford a shared apartment until I secured a job as palace bookkeeper.
In our fourth floor apartment, one room held my father and I. Two other bedrooms held two other families, and we shared a dining room.
The other two families didn't like me very much. So when I first saw the royal palace, I thought that it was so …. spacious. And grand.
A home for just one family beautiful enough to shame a sunset.
And I knew it was impossible for any family who sat on their ass for generations to deserve any of this. And everything they did proved me right.
Sinking their claws into the proletariat and watching them writhe, but gave none of them the right to even scream.
I asked where the servant's quarters were. "Outside," they said. And people dare call me too brutal. As if we would be worse than the alternative.
Now, Aijinkova is beautiful. Kind to the ones whose backs it is built upon. Our foreign relations are improving, and we are rebuilding.
You have not seen the outside, because of the quarantine, and the spoiled. The rebels—the radicals—try to poison us for a peace we already have.
